title: Integral of the Gaussian product density derivative
statement: Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $v>0$, let $c\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. Write $p_v(m,t)$ for the density of the real Gaussian with mean $m$ and variance $v$, and let $Z$ have independent coordinates with $Z_j\sim N(c_j,v)$. Then the integral, with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$, of $f(z)$ times the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)\frac{z_i-c_i}{v}p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$ equals the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb E[\frac{Z_i-c_i}{v}f(Z)]h_i$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$, $c,h\in\mathbb R^I$, and $Z\sim\bigotimes_iN(c_i,v)$, then $(\int f(z)A_v(c,z)\,dz)[h]=\sum_i\mathbb E[((Z_i-c_i)/v)f(Z)]h_i$.
